dataList.content: [Report No. 5A71-1. Routine Activity Record and Supporting Documentation. Filed by Outis, Representative of Wedge Office.]
Today, I took custody of the effects left behind by our partner Office.
The inventory runs to a stack of reports, a substantial number of contracts, several changes of clothes, and weapons kept in reserve...
Plus one Fixer.
I see no need to enter his name. There is no question of bringing him into this Office as an asset we could use; his temperament is altogether unsuited to this Office.
Equally, I cannot picture him making his way if turned out to fend for himself. He scarcely has the grit to fight for his life, let alone make a name for himself.
Fixer "A" of the Dawn Office. That will suffice.
Yes, Fixer A. For anyone who eventually cross-checks the Fixer death rolls, that should be identification enough.
I conducted a brief interview for the purpose of gathering intel.
I now have the sequence of events that transpired with our sister Office, the course they took... and an account of how they reached this deplorable outcome.
They had the edge over us in combat. Working alongside them had allowed us to shore up that weakness in our own capabilities...
Yet all that strength came to nothing for want of sound judgment. Still, I cannot deny some regret that we were unable to join them.
Their inability to show this... sentimental weakling the door without hesitation... may have been another symptom of the same failing.
Was the tea really worth keeping him on for? The ssanghwa-cha is exceptional, I grant that... but this is an Office, not a tearoom. A gifted tea-maker does not make that decision a sound one.
Softhearted to a fault. That was always the trouble with that old friend of mine...
... Returning to the purpose of this report: we were obliged to refuse our sister Office's request for assistance. The grounds for that refusal should also be placed on record.
The 8 o'clock Circus gave us no shortage of trouble.

I do not attribute that to the clown called the "ringmaster" of the Circus. His strength was nothing extraordinary. Had the encounter been confined to him and me, I doubt there would have been any great difficulty.
What complicated matters were the grotesque creatures described as his "friends"—that is, his troupe members.
A pattern in their strategy or tactics would at least have given us something to work with, but there was none. I could not even detect a common procedure guiding their actions.
Their next move was anyone's guess... A circus performance whose next show was nothing predictable, yes. It was well named, if nothing else. In every sense of the word.

One of our own Fixers had his body all but destroyed in the fighting. The attacker resembled a lion. I would provide more identifying details if I had them... but I was engaged elsewhere and didn't get a clear look at the entity.

For a time, I had considered the worst-case possibility: every Fixer under my command lost, and the Office's very survival in question... Little by little, however, we forced the enemy back and finally brought them to bay. Fortunate, perhaps...
That was when the ringmaster took several apparently higher-ranking troupe members and retreated. We were in no condition to give pursuit. Our own withdrawal left the contract unfinished.
We had, at least, taken out that life insurance in advance. It proved sufficient to restore the Fixer via the same body that had been cloned just in case...

What the policy could not offer, however, was the immediate restoration of physical abilities following the body transfer. That, I submit, is ample explanation for our inability to answer the request assistance.
Should the Office Credit Assessment Committee under the Hana Association choose to make an issue of this at a later date, I trust it will give these facts their due consideration.
The following two documents are appended in support:
One copy of the payment record and expense-reimbursement claim for Non-participating Safe Solution Fixer Indemnity Insurance, Type B.
One copy of the combat record for the elimination contract against the 8 o'clock Circus, as it is commonly known.
... Something tells me the 8 o'clock Circus still has a great deal of havoc left to wreak. It may be prudent to bring this to the Association's attention in a separate report.
I should attend to it once the next contract is concluded.
Ah, but one point needs putting beyond dispute.
No vengeance for our partner Office is involved here. Nor any desire to do a favor for that troublesome piece of salvage that had been their rookie member.
As should be abundantly clear, I am not in the habit of acting selflessly.
This is a job, plain and simple.
Of course, it is also a matter of paying my respects to an old friend, now deceased. That consideration, however, remains strictly secondary. Completing the contract always comes first.

Wedge Office's standing directive is to assess the situation at hand accurately and bring each contract to a swift, decisive conclusion. We are simply acting in accordance with that directive, as we always have.
... But enough of this. We should be getting underway with the contract.
I have had my fill of the sorry spectacle fidgeting in that corner: all nerves and impatience, waiting to be told when we will leave for the Library.
... Hm. That reminds me. One of the effects we collected was rather unusual.
Using it doesn't sit well with me. Still... perhaps that softhearted friend of mine left it for precisely that purpose.
As for where its user would land, I cannot say. But... I can hardly be expected to look after every last detail.
I will conclude my report here.
... Hm. Once we arrive at the Library, perhaps I will ask how thick that old friend's book turned out to be.
